boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Lake Forest College spaces for focused work, tutoring, reflection, recreation, and time with student groups, verified through current College pages.

cards.entity_name: Donnelley and Lee Library Study Rooms
cards.title: Reserve a Room for the Work That Needs a Door
cards.subtitle: Individual, collaborative, and group study inside Donnelley and Lee Library
cards.notes: Book a study room for group work or settle into a basement quiet zone; after-hours entry to the 24-hour area requires a College ID.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms and quiet zones support several different ways of studying.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College says the library provides individual, collaborative, and group study spaces; its basement has quiet zones and reservable rooms.
cards.source_title: Donnelley and Lee Library | Lake Forest College
cards.access_notes: The library lists daily building hours; its 24-hour computer lab and study area is limited to College students, faculty, and staff, with College ID required after hours.

cards.title: Pair a Library Session With a Café Table
cards.subtitle: First-floor work and refreshment space in Donnelley and Lee Library
cards.notes: Use the café side for a change of study setting and check the dining page before visiting, since service hours vary by weekday.
cards.short_summary: A named café inside the library offers another setting for breaks and study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College identifies Cyber Cafe on the library’s first floor and describes it as serving coffee drinks, juices, fruit, and baked goods.
cards.access_notes: Current academic-year service hours are posted on the dining page; Saturday service is listed as closed. Purchases are required for food and drinks.

cards.title: Claim a Booth Between Campus Commitments
cards.subtitle: Meeting rooms, downstairs tables, booths, and shared gathering areas
cards.notes: Try the downstairs tables or booths for informal work, or use an available meeting room when your group needs a defined place to gather.
cards.short_summary: The student center includes several practical settings for solo and group work.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s accessibility guidance says Mohr Student Center offers meeting rooms, downstairs tables and booths, and Calvin Durand Hall as places students can study.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to building operations and room availability; the source does not state that every meeting room is always open.

cards.title: Step Away for Quiet Reflection
cards.subtitle: A private reflection space in Mohr Student Commons
cards.notes: Use the room for prayer, meditation, or quiet reflection, and review the posted rules so the private shared environment works for everyone.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated room welcomes both religious and secular forms of reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College says the Interfaith Reflection Room welcomes all students, faculty, and staff for prayer, meditation, faith practice, or quiet reflection.
cards.source_title: Success and Support | Lake Forest College
cards.access_notes: Located in Mohr Student Commons. Follow the College’s linked rules of use and respect the room’s private, quiet purpose.

cards.title: Gather Around a Kitchen and Dining Table
cards.subtitle: Reservable collective space on South Campus
cards.notes: Contact CARE to check out the key, or reserve the house for a small student-group event that benefits from kitchen and dining space.
cards.short_summary: The South Campus house combines lounge seating, a kitchen, television, and dining space.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College describes the Intercultural House as a student hangout with a kitchen, TV, seating, dining area, and gender-neutral bathroom; groups may reserve it for small events.
cards.source_title: Success and Support | Lake Forest College
cards.access_notes: Students must contact CARE using the details on the source page to check out the key; small student-group events require a reservation.

cards.title: Bring the Problem Set to a Tutor
cards.subtitle: One-on-one and small-group quantitative support in Hotchkiss Hall
cards.notes: Schedule a session for an eligible course and bring the specific concept, notes, or assessment plan you want to work through with a tutor.
cards.short_summary: The QRC turns a study block into focused quantitative tutoring.
cards.evidence_claim: The Quantitative Resource Center provides one-on-one and small-group tutoring for specified math, economics, business, and finance courses.
cards.source_title: Quantitative Resource Center | Lake Forest College
cards.access_notes: Located on the lower level of Hotchkiss Hall. The current page lists weekday hours and directs students to the online scheduler for appointment availability.

cards.title: Use a Purpose-Built Place to Decompress
cards.subtitle: A sensory room in the CARE office
cards.notes: Visit the CARE office when you need a lower-stimulation pause, and ask staff about availability before counting on the room between classes.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated sensory environment offers students a campus place to reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College’s accessibility guidance specifically recommends the CARE office’s sensory room as a soothing campus space.
cards.access_notes: The source confirms the room and its intended use but does not publish walk-in hours; contact CARE to verify access and availability.

cards.title: Reserve a Structured Reset
cards.subtitle: Bookable relaxation space with a massage chair and sunlamp
cards.notes: Reserve a time through the student health portal when a scheduled quiet break would help; confirm current availability before heading over.
cards.short_summary: This reservable wellness room includes equipment intended for relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College says the Health and Wellness Relaxation Room has a massage chair and sunlamp and can be reserved through the student health portal.
cards.access_notes: Reservations are made through the Lake Forest student health portal; the public source does not provide room-specific operating hours.

cards.title: Fit Movement Into the Academic Day
cards.subtitle: Gym, track, courts, fitness areas, field house, and pool
cards.notes: Check the current facility schedule, choose the activity area you need, and allow for classes, practices, contests, or breaks that may affect access.
cards.short_summary: One building supports several forms of student exercise and recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College lists a gym, field house, weight room, cardio suite, track, handball courts, and pool at the Sports and Recreation Center.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Facilities Hours | Lake Forest College
cards.access_notes: Academic-year hours are posted by facility area. Pool classes and team practices may overlap with open swim, and schedules may change during breaks or events.

cards.title: Use the Rink During Open-Skate Hours
cards.subtitle: Weekday open skating for the College community
cards.notes: Bring appropriate skating gear and verify the facilities page before going, since open-skate access is limited to a posted weekday window.
cards.short_summary: The campus rink provides a defined midday recreation option during its operating season.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s current facilities page lists weekday open-skate hours at the Ice Rink for Lake Forest College students, faculty, and staff.
cards.source_title: On-Campus Facilities Hours | Lake Forest College
cards.access_notes: Open skate is listed Monday–Friday from noon to 3 p.m. for students, faculty, and staff; Saturday and Sunday are closed. Verify seasonal changes before visiting.

warnings: Coordinates and Google Maps URLs are null because exact entrances or room-level map pins were not verified from direct sources.
Access to several spaces is restricted to Lake Forest College students or the wider College community, and some rooms require a key, reservation, appointment, or College ID.
